454/* Utilities for converting from flags to delete policies and vice versa. */
455#define ECS_ID_ON_DELETE(flags) \
456 ((ecs_entity_t[]){0, EcsRemove, EcsDelete, 0, EcsPanic}\
457 [((flags) & EcsIdOnDeleteMask)])
458#define ECS_ID_ON_DELETE_TARGET(flags) ECS_ID_ON_DELETE(flags >> 3)
459#define ECS_ID_ON_DELETE_FLAG(id) (1u << ((id) - EcsRemove))
460#define ECS_ID_ON_DELETE_TARGET_FLAG(id) (1u << (3 + ((id) - EcsRemove)))
461
462/* Utilities for converting from flags to instantiate policies and vice versa. */
463#define ECS_ID_ON_INSTANTIATE(flags) \
464 ((ecs_entity_t[]){EcsOverride, EcsOverride, EcsInherit, 0, EcsDontInherit}\
465 [(((flags) & EcsIdOnInstantiateMask) >> 6)])
466#define ECS_ID_ON_INSTANTIATE_FLAG(id) (1u << (6 + ((id) - EcsOverride)))

667 * the format of __PRETTY_FUNCTION__, which enum reflection depends on. */

669 #if defined(__APPLE__)

691/* Ignored warnings */
692#if defined(ECS_TARGET_CLANG)
693/* Ignore unknown options so we don't have to care about the compiler version. */
694#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wunknown-warning-option"
695/* Warns for double or redundant semicolons. There are legitimate cases where a
696 * semicolon after an empty statement is useful, for example, after a macro that
697 * is replaced with a code block. With this warning enabled, semicolons would
698 * only have to be added after macros that are not code blocks, which in some
699 * cases isn't possible as the implementation of a macro can be different in
700 * debug/release mode. */
701#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wextra-semi-stmt"
702/* This is valid in C99, and Flecs must be compiled as C99. */
703#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wdeclaration-after-statement"
704/* Clang attribute to detect fallthrough isn't supported on older versions.
705 * Implicit fallthrough is still detected by gcc and ignored with "fall through"
706 * comments. */
707#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wimplicit-fallthrough"
708/* This warning prevents adding a default case when all enum constants are part
709 * of the switch. In C, however, an enum type can assume any value in the range of
710 * the type, and this warning makes it harder to catch invalid enum values. */
711#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wcovered-switch-default"
712/* This warning prevents some casts of function results to a different kind of
713 * type, e.g., casting an int result to double. Not very useful in practice, as
714 * it just forces the code to assign to a variable first, then cast. */
715#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wbad-function-cast"
716/* Format strings can be passed down from other functions. */
717#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wformat-nonliteral"
718/* Useful, but not reliable enough. It can incorrectly flag macros as unused
719 * in standalone builds. */
720#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wunused-macros"
721/* This warning gets thrown by clang even when the code is handling all case
722 * values but not all cases (for example, when the switch contains a LastValue
723 * case). Adding a "default" case fixes the warning, but silences future
724 * warnings about unhandled cases, which is worse. */
725#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wswitch-default"
726#if __clang_major__ == 13
727/* clang 13 can throw this warning for a macro in ctype.h. */
728#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wreserved-identifier"
729#endif
730/* Filenames aren't consistent across targets as they can use different casing
731 * (e.g., WinSock2 vs. winsock2). */
732#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wnonportable-system-include-path"
733/* Very difficult to work around this warning in C, especially for an ECS. */
734#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wunsafe-buffer-usage"
735/* This warning gets thrown when trying to cast a pointer returned from dlproc. */
736#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wcast-function-type-strict"
737/* This warning can get thrown for expressions that evaluate to constants
738 * in debug/release mode. */
739#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wconstant-logical-operand"
740/* With soft asserts enabled, the code won't abort, which in some cases means
741 * code paths are reached where values are uninitialized. */
742#ifdef FLECS_SOFT_ASSERT
743#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wsometimes-uninitialized"
744#endif
745
746/* Allows for enum reflection support on legacy compilers. */
747#if __clang_major__ < 16
748#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wenum-constexpr-conversion"
749#endif
750
751#elif defined(ECS_TARGET_GNU)
752#ifndef __cplusplus
753#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wdeclaration-after-statement"
754#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wbad-function-cast"
755#endif
756#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wformat-nonliteral"
757#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wunused-macros"
758/* This warning gets thrown *sometimes* when not all members for a struct are
759 * provided in an initializer. Flecs heavily relies on descriptor structs that
760 * only require partial initialization, so this warning isn't useful.
761 * It doesn't introduce any safety issues (fields are guaranteed to be 0
762 * initialized), and later versions of gcc (>=11) seem to no longer throw this
763 * warning. */
764#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wmissing-field-initializers"
765/* Produces false positives in addons/cpp/delegate.hpp. */
766#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Warray-bounds"
767/* Produces false positives in queries/src/cache.c. */
768#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wstringop-overflow"
769#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wrestrict"
770
771#elif defined(ECS_TARGET_MSVC)
772/* Recursive on all control paths, the function will cause runtime stack overflow.
773 * This warning is incorrectly thrown on enum reflection code. */
774#pragma warning(disable: 4717)
775#endif
776
777/* Allows for enum reflection support on legacy compilers. */
778#if defined(__GNUC__) && __GNUC__ <= 10
779#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wconversion"
780#endif

879/* Bitset type that can store exactly as many bits as there are terms. */

882/* Utility macros for setting/clearing termset bits. */
883#define ECS_TERMSET_SET(set, flag) ((set) |= (ecs_termset_t)(flag))
884#define ECS_TERMSET_CLEAR(set, flag) ((set) &= (ecs_termset_t)~(flag))
885#define ECS_TERMSET_COND(set, flag, cond) ((cond) \
886 ? (ECS_TERMSET_SET(set, flag)) \
887 : (ECS_TERMSET_CLEAR(set, flag)))

897/* Alignment macros:
898 * - Use alignof in C++
899 * - Use _Alignof in C11 and above
900 * - Use __alignof__ on 64 bit platforms on clang/gcc
901 * - Use struct trick on other compilers/32 bit
902 *
903 * The reason the code doesn't use the struct trick everywhere is because this
904 * can cause ASAN errors (runtime error: member access within null pointer).
905 *
906 * The reason why the clang/gcc __alignof__ feature is not used on 32 bit, is
907 * because its behavior is different than C++:
908 *
909 * __alignof__(uint64_t) == 8 on 32-bit platforms
910 * alignof(uint64_t) == 4 on 32-bit platforms
911 *
912 * typedef struct {
913 * uint64_t value;
914 * } Foo;
915 *
916 * __alignof__(Foo) == 4 on 32-bit platforms
917 * alignof(Foo) == 4 on 32-bit platforms
918 */
919#ifdef __cplusplus
920#define ECS_ALIGNOF(T) static_cast<int64_t>(alignof(T))
921#elif defined(ECS_TARGET_MSVC)
922#define ECS_ALIGNOF(T) (int64_t)__alignof(T)
923#else
924#define ECS_ALIGNOF(T) ((int64_t)(size_t)&((struct { char c; T d; } *)0)->d)
925#if defined(ECS_TARGET_GNU) || defined(ECS_TARGET_CLANG)
926#if __SIZEOF_POINTER__ == 8
927#undef ECS_ALIGNOF
928#define ECS_ALIGNOF(T) (int64_t)__alignof__(T)
929#endif
930#endif
931#endif

1078/* Constructor/Destructor convenience macro */
1079#define ECS_XTOR_IMPL(type, postfix, var, ...)\
1080 void type##_##postfix(\
1081 void *_ptr,\
1082 int32_t _count,\
1083 const ecs_type_info_t *type_info)\
1084 {\
1085 (void)_ptr;\
1086 (void)_count;\
1087 (void)type_info;\
1088 for (int32_t i = 0; i < _count; i ++) {\
1089 type *var = &((type*)_ptr)[i];\
1090 (void)var;\
1091 __VA_ARGS__\
1092 }\
1093 }
1094
1095/* Copy convenience macro */
1096#define ECS_COPY_IMPL(type, dst_var, src_var, ...)\
1097 void type##_##copy(\
1098 void *_dst_ptr,\
1099 const void *_src_ptr,\
1100 int32_t _count,\
1101 const ecs_type_info_t *type_info)\
1102 {\
1103 (void)_dst_ptr;\
1104 (void)_src_ptr;\
1105 (void)_count;\
1106 (void)type_info;\
1107 for (int32_t i = 0; i < _count; i ++) {\
1108 type *dst_var = &((type*)_dst_ptr)[i];\
1109 const type *src_var = &((const type*)_src_ptr)[i];\
1110 (void)dst_var;\
1111 (void)src_var;\
1112 __VA_ARGS__\
1113 }\
1114 }
1115
1116/* Move convenience macro */
1117#define ECS_MOVE_IMPL(type, dst_var, src_var, ...)\
1118 void type##_##move(\
1119 void *_dst_ptr,\
1120 void *_src_ptr,\
1121 int32_t _count,\
1122 const ecs_type_info_t *type_info)\
1123 {\
1124 (void)_dst_ptr;\
1125 (void)_src_ptr;\
1126 (void)_count;\
1127 (void)type_info;\
1128 for (int32_t i = 0; i < _count; i ++) {\
1129 type *dst_var = &((type*)_dst_ptr)[i];\
1130 type *src_var = &((type*)_src_ptr)[i];\
1131 (void)dst_var;\
1132 (void)src_var;\
1133 __VA_ARGS__\
1134 }\
1135 }
1136
1137#define ECS_HOOK_IMPL(type, func, var, ...)\
1138 void func(ecs_iter_t *_it)\
1139 {\
1140 type *field_data = ecs_field(_it, type, 0);\
1141 for (int32_t i = 0; i < _it->count; i ++) {\
1142 ecs_entity_t entity = _it->entities[i];\
1143 type *var = &field_data[i];\
1144 (void)entity;\
1145 (void)var;\
1146 __VA_ARGS__\
1147 }\
1148 }

3694 ecs_os_api_mutex_lock_t mutex_lock_;
3695 ecs_os_api_mutex_lock_t mutex_unlock_;

4546/* Flags that can be used to check which hooks a type has set */
4547#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 0)
4548#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_DTOR ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 1)
4549#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 2)
4550#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 3)
4551#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY_CTOR ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 4)
4552#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_CTOR ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 5)
4553#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR_MOVE_DTOR ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 6)
4554#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_DTOR ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 7)
4555#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CMP ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 8)
4556#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_EQUALS ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 9)
4557
4558/* Flags that can be used to set/check which hooks of a type are invalid */
4559#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 10)
4560#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_DTOR_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 12)
4561#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 13)
4562#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 14)
4563#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY_CTOR_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 15)
4564#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_CTOR_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 16)
4565#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR_MOVE_DTOR_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 17)
4566#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_DTOR_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 18)
4567#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CMP_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 19)
4568#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_EQUALS_ILLEGAL ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 20)
4569
4570/* Internal debug flag that indicates type hooks have been invoked */
4571#define ECS_TYPE_HOOK_IN_USE ECS_CAST(ecs_flags32_t, 1 << 21)
4572
4573/* All valid hook flags */
4574#define ECS_TYPE_HOOKS (ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_DTOR|\
4575 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY_CTOR|\
4576 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_CTOR|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR_MOVE_DTOR|\
4577 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_DTOR|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CMP|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_EQUALS)
4578
4579/* All invalid hook flags */
4580#define ECS_TYPE_HOOKS_ILLEGAL (ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR_ILLEGAL|\
4581 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_DTOR_ILLEGAL|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY_ILLEGAL|\
4582 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_ILLEGAL|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_COPY_CTOR_ILLEGAL|\
4583 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_CTOR_ILLEGAL|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR_MOVE_DTOR_ILLEGAL|\
4584 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_MOVE_DTOR_ILLEGAL|ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CMP_ILLEGAL|\
4585 ECS_TYPE_HOOK_EQUALS_ILLEGAL)
4586struct ecs_type_hooks_t {
4587 ecs_xtor_t ctor;
4588 ecs_xtor_t dtor;
4589 ecs_copy_t copy;
4590 ecs_move_t move;
4593 ecs_copy_t copy_ctor;
4594
4596 ecs_move_t move_ctor;
4597
4602 ecs_move_t ctor_move_dtor;
4603
4608 ecs_move_t move_dtor;
4609
4611 ecs_cmp_t cmp;
4612
4614 ecs_equals_t equals;
4615
4620 ecs_flags32_t flags;
4621
4624 ecs_iter_action_t on_add;
4625
4629 ecs_iter_action_t on_set;
4630
4634 ecs_iter_action_t on_remove;
4635
4640 ecs_iter_action_t on_replace;
4641
4642 void *ctx;
4643 void *binding_ctx;
4644 void *lifecycle_ctx;
4646 ecs_ctx_free_t ctx_free;
4647 ecs_ctx_free_t binding_ctx_free;
4648 ecs_ctx_free_t lifecycle_ctx_free;
4649};

4759
4760 /* Storage for iterator fields. */

4768typedef struct ecs_query_op_profile_t {
4769 int32_t count[2]; /* 0 = enter, 1 = redo */

4771
4773typedef struct ecs_query_iter_t {
4774 struct ecs_var_t *vars; /* Variable storage. */
4775 const struct ecs_query_var_t *query_vars; /* Query variable metadata. */
4776 const struct ecs_query_op_t *ops; /* Query plan operations. */
4777 struct ecs_query_op_ctx_t *op_ctx; /* Operation-specific state. */
4778 uint64_t *written;
4779
4780 /* Cached iteration. */
4781 ecs_query_cache_group_t *group; /* Currently iterated group. */
4782 ecs_vec_t *tables; /* Currently iterated table vector (vec<ecs_query_cache_match_t>). */
4783 ecs_vec_t *all_tables; /* Different from .tables if iterating wildcard matches (vec<ecs_query_cache_match_t>). */
4784 ecs_query_cache_match_t *elem; /* Current cache entry. */
4785 int32_t cur, all_cur; /* Indices into tables and all_tables. */
4786
4787 ecs_query_op_profile_t *profile;
4788
4789 int16_t op; /* Currently iterated query plan operation (index into ops). */
4790 bool iter_single_group;
4791} ecs_query_iter_t;
4792
4793/* Private iterator data. Used by iterator implementations to keep track of
4794 * progress and to provide built-in storage. */
4795typedef struct ecs_iter_private_t {
4796 union {
4797 ecs_query_iter_t query;
4798 ecs_page_iter_t page;
4799 ecs_worker_iter_t worker;
4800 ecs_each_iter_t each;
4801 } iter; /* Iterator-specific data. */
4802
4803 void *entity_iter; /* Query applied after matching a table. */
4804 ecs_stack_cursor_t *stack_cursor; /* Stack cursor to restore to. */
4805} ecs_iter_private_t;
4806
4807/* Data structures that store the command queue. */

4810 ecs_stack_t stack; /* Temp memory used by deferred commands. */
4811 ecs_sparse_t entries; /* <entity, op_entry_t> - command batching. */
4812} ecs_commands_t;

5035/* Suspend and resume read-only state. To fully support implicit registration of
5036 * components, it should be possible to register components while the world is
5037 * in read-only mode. It is not uncommon that a component is used first from
5038 * within a system, which is often run while in read-only mode.
5039 *
5040 * Suspending read-only mode is only allowed when the world is not multithreaded.
5041 * When a world is multithreaded, it is not safe to (even temporarily) leave
5042 * read-only mode, so a multithreaded application should always explicitly
5043 * register components in advance.
5044 *
5045 * These operations also suspend deferred mode.
5046 *
5047 * Functions are public to support language bindings.
5048 */
5049typedef struct ecs_suspend_readonly_state_t {
5050 bool is_readonly;
5051 bool is_deferred;
5052 bool cmd_flushing;
5053 int32_t defer_count;
5054 ecs_entity_t scope;
5055 ecs_entity_t with;
5056 ecs_commands_t cmd_stack[2];
5057 ecs_commands_t *cmd;
5058 ecs_stage_t *stage;
5059} ecs_suspend_readonly_state_t;
5060

5230#ifdef __cplusplus
5231#define ECS_OFFSET(o, offset) reinterpret_cast<void*>((reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(o)) + (static_cast<uintptr_t>(offset)))
5232#else
5233#define ECS_OFFSET(o, offset) (void*)(((uintptr_t)(o)) + ((uintptr_t)(offset)))
5234#endif
5235#define ECS_OFFSET_T(o, T) ECS_OFFSET(o, ECS_SIZEOF(T))
5236
5237#define ECS_ELEM(ptr, size, index) ECS_OFFSET(ptr, (size) * (index))
5238#define ECS_ELEM_T(o, T, index) ECS_ELEM(o, ECS_SIZEOF(T), index)
5239
5241#define ECS_BIT_SET(flags, bit) (flags) |= (bit)
5242#define ECS_BIT_CLEAR(flags, bit) (flags) &= ~(bit)
5243#define ECS_BIT_COND(flags, bit, cond) ((cond) \
5244 ? (ECS_BIT_SET(flags, bit)) \
5245 : (ECS_BIT_CLEAR(flags, bit)))
5246
5247#define ECS_BIT_CLEAR16(flags, bit) (flags) &= (ecs_flags16_t)~(bit)
5248#define ECS_BIT_COND16(flags, bit, cond) ((cond) \
5249 ? (ECS_BIT_SET(flags, bit)) \
5250 : (ECS_BIT_CLEAR16(flags, bit)))
5251
5252#define ECS_BIT_IS_SET(flags, bit) ((flags) & (bit))
5253
5254#define ECS_BIT_SETN(flags, n) ECS_BIT_SET(flags, 1llu << n)
5255#define ECS_BIT_CLEARN(flags, n) ECS_BIT_CLEAR(flags, 1llu << n)
5256#define ECS_BIT_CONDN(flags, n, cond) ECS_BIT_COND(flags, 1llu << n, cond)
5257

12371#define ECS_SORT_TABLE_WITH_COMPARE(id, op_name, compare_fn, ...) \
12372 static int32_t ECS_CONCAT(op_name, _partition)( \
12373 ecs_world_t *world, \
12374 ecs_table_t *table, \
12375 ecs_entity_t *entities, \
12376 void *ptr, \
12377 int32_t elem_size, \
12378 int32_t lo, \
12379 int32_t hi, \
12380 ecs_order_by_action_t order_by) \
12381 { \
12382 (void)(order_by); \
12383 int32_t p = (hi + lo) / 2; \
12384 void *pivot = ECS_ELEM(ptr, elem_size, p); \
12385 ecs_entity_t pivot_e = entities[p]; \
12386 int32_t i = lo - 1, j = hi + 1; \
12387 void *el; \
12388 repeat: \
12389 { \
12390 do { \
12391 i ++; \
12392 el = ECS_ELEM(ptr, elem_size, i); \
12393 } while ( compare_fn(entities[i], el, pivot_e, pivot) < 0); \
12394 do { \
12395 j --; \
12396 el = ECS_ELEM(ptr, elem_size, j); \
12397 } while ( compare_fn(entities[j], el, pivot_e, pivot) > 0); \
12398 if (i >= j) { \
12399 return j; \
12400 } \
12401 ecs_table_swap_rows(world, table, i, j); \
12402 if (p == i) { \
12403 pivot = ECS_ELEM(ptr, elem_size, j); \
12404 pivot_e = entities[j]; \
12405 } else if (p == j) { \
12406 pivot = ECS_ELEM(ptr, elem_size, i); \
12407 pivot_e = entities[i]; \
12408 } \
12409 goto repeat; \
12410 } \
12411 } \
12412 __VA_ARGS__ void op_name( \
12413 ecs_world_t *world, \
12414 ecs_table_t *table, \
12415 ecs_entity_t *entities, \
12416 void *ptr, \
12417 int32_t size, \
12418 int32_t lo, \
12419 int32_t hi, \
12420 ecs_order_by_action_t order_by) \
12421 { \
12422 if ((hi - lo) < 1) { \
12423 return; \
12424 } \
12425 int32_t p = ECS_CONCAT(op_name, _partition)(world, table, entities, ptr, size, lo, hi, order_by); \
12426 op_name(world, table, entities, ptr, size, lo, p, order_by); \
12427 op_name(world, table, entities, ptr, size, p + 1, hi, order_by); \
12428 }
12429
12441#define ECS_SORT_TABLE(id, ...) \
12442 ECS_SORT_TABLE_WITH_COMPARE(id, ecs_sort_table(id), ecs_compare(id), __VA_ARGS__)
12443
12454#define ECS_COMPARE(id, ...) \
12455 int ecs_compare(id)(ecs_entity_t e1, const void* ptr1, ecs_entity_t e2, const void* ptr2) { \
12456 __VA_ARGS__ \
12457 }

14093#define ECS_PIPELINE_DEFINE(world, id_, ...) \
14094 { \
14095 ecs_pipeline_desc_t desc = {0}; \
14096 ecs_entity_desc_t edesc = {0}; \
14097 edesc.id = id_;\
14098 edesc.name = #id_;\
14099 desc.entity = ecs_entity_init(world, &edesc);\
14100 desc.query.expr = #__VA_ARGS__; \
14101 id_ = ecs_pipeline_init(world, &desc); \
14102 ecs_id(id_) = id_;\
14103 } \
14104 ecs_assert(id_ != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER, "failed to create pipeline");
14105
14113#define ECS_PIPELINE(world, id, ...) \
14114 ecs_entity_t id = 0, ecs_id(id) = 0; ECS_PIPELINE_DEFINE(world, id, __VA_ARGS__);\
14115 (void)id;\
14116 (void)ecs_id(id);
14117
14121#define ecs_pipeline(world, ...)\
14122 ecs_pipeline_init(world, &(ecs_pipeline_desc_t) __VA_ARGS__ )
14123
14124#endif

14586#define ECS_SYSTEM_DEFINE(world, id_, phase_, ...) \
14587 { \
14588 ecs_system_desc_t desc = {0}; \
14589 ecs_entity_desc_t edesc = {0}; \
14590 edesc.id = ecs_id(id_);\
14591 edesc.name = #id_;\
14592 desc.entity = ecs_entity_init(world, &edesc);\
14593 desc.query.expr = #__VA_ARGS__; \
14594 desc.phase = phase_; \
14595 desc.callback = id_; \
14596 ecs_id(id_) = ecs_system_init(world, &desc); \
14597 } \
14598 ecs_assert(ecs_id(id_) != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER, "failed to create system %s", #id_)
14599
14608#define ECS_SYSTEM(world, id, phase, ...) \
14609 ecs_entity_t ecs_id(id) = 0; ECS_SYSTEM_DEFINE(world, id, phase, __VA_ARGS__);\
14610 ecs_entity_t id = ecs_id(id);\
14611 (void)ecs_id(id);\
14612 (void)id
14613
14632#define ecs_system(world, ...)\

19266
19267/* Macro that controls behavior of API. Usually set in module header. When the
19268 * macro is not defined, it defaults to IMPL. */
19269
19270/* Define variables used by reflection utilities. This should only be defined
19271 * by the module itself, not by the code importing the module. */
19272/* #define ECS_META_IMPL IMPL */
19273
19274/* Don't define variables used by reflection utilities, but still declare the
19275 * variable for the component ID. This enables the reflection utilities to be
19276 * used for global component variables, even if no reflection is used. */
19277/* #define ECS_META_IMPL DECLARE */
19278
19279/* Don't define variables used by reflection utilities. This generates an extern
19280 * variable for the component identifier. */
19281/* #define ECS_META_IMPL EXTERN */
19282
19284#define ECS_META_COMPONENT(world, name)\
19285 ECS_COMPONENT_DEFINE(world, name);\

19622#define ECS_FUNC_NAME __PRETTY_FUNCTION__
19623#elif defined(__GNUC__)

19626#define ECS_FUNC_NAME __PRETTY_FUNCTION__
19627#elif defined(_WIN32)
19628#define ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(type, name) ((sizeof(#type) + sizeof(" __cdecl flecs::_::<") + sizeof(#name)) - 3u)
19629#define ECS_FUNC_NAME_BACK (sizeof(">(void)") - 1u)
19630#define ECS_FUNC_NAME __FUNCSIG__
19631#else
19632#error "implicit component registration not supported"
19633#endif
19634
19635#define ECS_FUNC_TYPE_LEN(type, name, str)\
19636 (flecs::string::length(str) - (ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(type, name) + ECS_FUNC_NAME_BACK))
19637
19638#endif

20125// C++ utilities
20126
20127// Macros so that C++ new calls can allocate using ecs_os_api memory allocation functions.
20128// Rationale:
20129// - Using macros here instead of a templated function because clients might override
20130// ecs_os_malloc to contain extra debug info like source tracking location. Using a
20131// template function in that scenario would collapse all source locations into said
20132// function vs. the actual call site.
20133// - FLECS_PLACEMENT_NEW(): exists to remove any naked new calls and make it easy to identify any
20134// regressions by grepping for new/delete.
20135
20136#define FLECS_PLACEMENT_NEW(_ptr, _type) ::new(flecs::_::placement_new_tag, _ptr) _type
20137#define FLECS_NEW(_type) FLECS_PLACEMENT_NEW(ecs_os_malloc(sizeof(_type)), _type)
20138#define FLECS_DELETE(_ptr) \
20139 do { \
20140 if (_ptr) { \
20141 flecs::_::destruct_obj(_ptr); \
20142 ecs_os_free(_ptr); \
20143 } \
20144 } while (false)
20145
20146/* Faster (compile-time) alternatives to std::move / std::forward. From:
20147 * https://www.foonathan.net/2020/09/move-forward/
20148 */
20149
20150#define FLECS_MOV(...) \
20151 static_cast<flecs::remove_reference_t<decltype(__VA_ARGS__)>&&>(__VA_ARGS__)
20152
20153#define FLECS_FWD(...) \
20154 static_cast<decltype(__VA_ARGS__)&&>(__VA_ARGS__)
20155

20157{
20158
20159namespace _
20160{
20161
20163struct placement_new_tag_t{};
20165constexpr placement_new_tag_t placement_new_tag{};
20167template<class Ty> inline void destruct_obj(Ty* _ptr) { _ptr->~Ty(); }
20169template<class Ty> inline void free_obj(void* _ptr) {
20170 if (_ptr) {
20171 destruct_obj(static_cast<Ty*>(_ptr));
20172 ecs_os_free(_ptr);
20173 }
20174}

20184
20185inline void* operator new(size_t, flecs::_::placement_new_tag_t, void* _ptr) noexcept { return _ptr; }
20186inline void operator delete(void*, flecs::_::placement_new_tag_t, void*) noexcept { }

20307template <typename T>
20308struct array_iterator
20309{
20311 explicit array_iterator(T* value, int index) {
20312 value_ = value;
20313 index_ = index;
20314 }
20315
20317 bool operator!=(array_iterator const& other) const
20318 {
20319 return index_ != other.index_;
20320 }
20321
20323 T & operator*() const
20324 {
20325 return value_[index_];
20326 }
20327
20329 array_iterator& operator++()
20330 {
20331 ++index_;
20332 return *this;
20333 }
20334
20335private:
20336 T* value_;
20337 int index_;
20338};

20341template <typename T, size_t Size, class Enable = void>
20342struct array final { };
20343
20345template <typename T, size_t Size>
20346struct array<T, Size, enable_if_t<Size != 0> > final {
20348 array() {};
20349
20351 array(const T (&elems)[Size]) {
20352 int i = 0;
20353 for (auto it = this->begin(); it != this->end(); ++ it) {
20354 *it = elems[i ++];
20355 }
20356 }
20357
20359 T& operator[](int index) {
20360 return array_[index];
20361 }
20362
20364 T& operator[](size_t index) {
20365 return array_[index];
20366 }
20367
20369 array_iterator<T> begin() {
20370 return array_iterator<T>(array_, 0);
20371 }
20372
20374 array_iterator<T> end() {
20375 return array_iterator<T>(array_, Size);
20376 }
20377
20379 size_t size() {
20380 return Size;
20381 }
20382
20384 T* ptr() {
20385 return array_;
20386 }
20387
20389 template <typename Func>
20390 void each(const Func& func) {
20391 for (auto& elem : *this) {
20392 func(elem);
20393 }
20394 }
20395
20396private:
20397 T array_[Size];
20398};
20399
20401template<typename T, size_t Size>
20402array<T, Size> to_array(const T (&elems)[Size]) {
20403 return array<T, Size>(elems);
20404}
20405
20407template <typename T, size_t Size>
20408struct array<T, Size, enable_if_t<Size == 0>> final {
20410 array() {};
20412 array(const T* (&elems)) { (void)elems; }
20414 T operator[](size_t index) { ecs_os_abort(); (void)index; return T(); }
20416 array_iterator<T> begin() { return array_iterator<T>(nullptr, 0); }
20418 array_iterator<T> end() { return array_iterator<T>(nullptr, 0); }
20419
20421 size_t size() {
20422 return 0;
20423 }
20424
20426 T* ptr() {
20427 return NULL;
20428 }
20429};

20442struct string {
20444 explicit string()
20445 : str_(nullptr)
20446 , const_str_("")
20447 , length_(0) { }
20448
20450 explicit string(char *str)
20451 : str_(str)
20452 , const_str_(str ? str : "")
20453 , length_(str ? ecs_os_strlen(str) : 0) { }
20454
20456 ~string() {
20457 // If flecs is included in a binary but is not used, it is possible that
20458 // the OS API is not initialized. Calling ecs_os_free in that case could
20459 // crash the application during exit. However, if a string has been set
20460 // flecs has been used, and OS API should have been initialized.
20461 if (str_) {
20462 ecs_os_free(str_);
20463 }
20464 }
20465
20467 string(string&& str) noexcept {
20468 ecs_os_free(str_);
20469 str_ = str.str_;
20470 const_str_ = str.const_str_;
20471 length_ = str.length_;
20472 str.str_ = nullptr;
20473 }
20474
20476 operator const char*() const {
20477 return const_str_;
20478 }
20479
20481 string& operator=(string&& str) noexcept {
20482 ecs_os_free(str_);
20483 str_ = str.str_;
20484 const_str_ = str.const_str_;
20485 length_ = str.length_;
20486 str.str_ = nullptr;
20487 return *this;
20488 }
20489
20491 string& operator=(const string& str) = delete;
20493 string(const string& str) = delete;
20494
20496 bool operator==(const flecs::string& str) const {
20497 if (str.const_str_ == const_str_) {
20498 return true;
20499 }
20500
20501 if (!const_str_ || !str.const_str_) {
20502 return false;
20503 }
20504
20505 if (str.length_ != length_) {
20506 return false;
20507 }
20508
20509 return ecs_os_strcmp(str, const_str_) == 0;
20510 }
20511
20513 bool operator!=(const flecs::string& str) const {
20514 return !(*this == str);
20515 }
20516
20518 bool operator==(const char *str) const {
20519 if (const_str_ == str) {
20520 return true;
20521 }
20522
20523 if (!const_str_ || !str) {
20524 return false;
20525 }
20526
20527 return ecs_os_strcmp(str, const_str_) == 0;
20528 }
20529
20531 bool operator!=(const char *str) const {
20532 return !(*this == str);
20533 }
20534
20536 const char* c_str() const {
20537 return const_str_;
20538 }
20539
20541 std::size_t length() const {
20542 return static_cast<std::size_t>(length_);
20543 }
20544
20546 template <size_t N>
20547 static constexpr size_t length( char const (&)[N] ) {
20548 return N - 1;
20549 }
20550
20552 std::size_t size() const {
20553 return length();
20554 }
20555
20557 void clear() {
20558 ecs_os_free(str_);
20559 str_ = nullptr;
20560 const_str_ = nullptr;
20561 }
20562
20564 bool contains(const char *substr) {
20565 if (const_str_) {
20566 return strstr(const_str_, substr) != nullptr;
20567 } else {
20568 return false;
20569 }
20570 }
20571
20572protected:
20580 string(const char *str)
20581 : str_(nullptr)
20582 , const_str_(str ? str : "")
20583 , length_(str ? ecs_os_strlen(str) : 0) { }
20584
20585 char *str_ = nullptr;
20586 const char *const_str_;
20587 ecs_size_t length_;
20588};
20589
20596struct string_view : string {
20598 explicit string_view(const char *str)
20599 : string(str) { }
20600};

20729#if defined(ECS_TARGET_CLANG)
20730#if ECS_CLANG_VERSION < 13
20731template <typename E, E C>
20732constexpr bool enum_constant_is_valid() {
20733 return !((
20734 (ECS_FUNC_NAME[ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(bool, enum_constant_is_valid) +
20735 enum_type_len<E>() + 6 /* ', C = ' */] >= '0') &&
20736 (ECS_FUNC_NAME[ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(bool, enum_constant_is_valid) +
20737 enum_type_len<E>() + 6 /* ', C = ' */] <= '9')) ||
20738 (ECS_FUNC_NAME[ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(bool, enum_constant_is_valid) +
20739 enum_type_len<E>() + 6 /* ', C = ' */] == '-'));
20740}
20741#else
20742template <typename E, E C>
20743constexpr bool enum_constant_is_valid() {
20744 return (ECS_FUNC_NAME[ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(bool, enum_constant_is_valid) +
20745 enum_type_len<E>() + 6 /* ', C = ' */] != '(');
20746}
20747#endif
20748#elif defined(ECS_TARGET_GNU)
20749template <typename E, E C>
20750constexpr bool enum_constant_is_valid() {
20751 return (ECS_FUNC_NAME[ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(constexpr bool, enum_constant_is_valid) +
20752 enum_type_len<E>() + 8 /* ', E C = ' */] != '(');
20753}
20754#else
20755template <size_t N>
20756constexpr size_t enum_template_arg_separator(
20757 const char (&func_name)[N],
20758 size_t pos,
20759 size_t end,
20760 size_t depth = 0)
20761{
20762 return pos >= end
20763 ? end
20764 : func_name[pos] == '<'
20765 ? enum_template_arg_separator(func_name, pos + 1, end, depth + 1)
20766 : func_name[pos] == '>'
20767 ? enum_template_arg_separator(
20768 func_name, pos + 1, end, depth ? depth - 1 : 0)
20769 : (func_name[pos] == ',' && !depth)
20770 ? pos
20771 : enum_template_arg_separator(
20772 func_name, pos + 1, end, depth);
20773}
20774
20775/* Use a different trick on MSVC, since it uses a hexadecimal representation for
20776 * invalid enum constants. We can leverage that MSVC inserts a C-style cast
20777 * into the name. Find the template argument separator structurally instead of
20778 * relying on the exact spelling of __FUNCSIG__ for the enum type. */
20779template <typename E, E C>
20780constexpr bool enum_constant_is_valid() {
20781 return enum_template_arg_separator(
20782 ECS_FUNC_NAME,
20783 ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(bool, enum_constant_is_valid),
20784 sizeof(ECS_FUNC_NAME) - ECS_FUNC_NAME_BACK - 1u) <
20785 (sizeof(ECS_FUNC_NAME) - ECS_FUNC_NAME_BACK - 1u) &&
20786 ECS_FUNC_NAME[enum_template_arg_separator(
20787 ECS_FUNC_NAME,
20788 ECS_FUNC_NAME_FRONT(bool, enum_constant_is_valid),
20789 sizeof(ECS_FUNC_NAME) - ECS_FUNC_NAME_BACK - 1u) + 1u] != '(';
20790}
20791#endif
20792
20794template <typename E, underlying_type_t<E> C>
20795constexpr bool enum_constant_is_valid_wrap() {
20796 return enum_constant_is_valid<E, flecs_enum_cast(E, C)>();
20797}
20798
20800template <typename E, E C>
20801struct enum_is_valid {
20802 static constexpr bool value = enum_constant_is_valid<E, C>();
20803};

20806template <typename E, E C>
20807static const char* enum_constant_to_name() {
20808 static const size_t len = ECS_FUNC_TYPE_LEN(
20809 const char*, enum_constant_to_name, ECS_FUNC_NAME);
20810 static char result[len + 1] = {};
20811 return ecs_cpp_get_constant_name(
20812 result, ECS_FUNC_NAME, string::length(ECS_FUNC_NAME),
20813 ECS_FUNC_NAME_BACK);
20814}

20826template <typename E, typename Handler>
20827struct enum_reflection {
20828 using U = underlying_type_t<E>;
20829
20846 template <U Low, U High, typename... Args>
20847 static constexpr U each_enum_range(U last_value, Args&... args) {
20848 return High - Low <= 1
20849 ? High == Low
20850 ? Handler::template handle_constant<Low>(last_value, args...)
20851 : Handler::template handle_constant<High>(
20852 Handler::template handle_constant<Low>(last_value, args...),
20853 args...)
20854 : each_enum_range<(Low + High) / 2 + 1, High>(
20855 each_enum_range<Low, (Low + High) / 2>(last_value, args...),
20856 args...
20857 );
20858 }
20859
20876 template <U Low, U High, typename... Args>
20877 static constexpr U each_mask_range(U last_value, Args&... args) {
20878 // If Low shares any bits with Current Flag, or if High is less
20879 // than/equal to Low (and High isn't negative because max-flag signed)
20880 return (Low & High) || (High <= Low && High != high_bit)
20881 ? last_value
20882 : Handler::template handle_constant<High>(
20883 each_mask_range<Low, ((High >> 1) & ~high_bit)>(last_value, args...),
20884 args...
20885 );
20886 }
20887
20900 template <U Value = static_cast<U>(FLECS_ENUM_MAX(E)), typename... Args>
20901 static constexpr U each_enum(Args&... args) {
20902 return each_mask_range<Value, high_bit>(
20903 each_enum_range<0, Value>(0, args...), args...);
20904 }
20905 /* To avoid warnings with bit manipulation, calculate the high bit with an
20906 unsigned type of the same size. */
20907 using UU = typename std::make_unsigned<U>::type;
20908 static const U high_bit =
20909 static_cast<U>(static_cast<UU>(1) << (sizeof(UU) * 8 - 1));
20910};
20911
20915template<typename T>
20916struct enum_constant {
20918 int32_t index;
20920 T value;
20922 T offset;
20924 const char *name;
20925};
20926
20928template <typename E>
20929struct enum_type {
20930private:
20931 using This = enum_type<E>;
20932 using U = underlying_type_t<E>;
20933
20937 struct reflection_count {
20938 template <U Value>
20939 static constexpr U handle_constant(U last_value) {
20940 if constexpr (enum_constant_is_valid_wrap<E, Value>()) {
20941 return 1 + last_value;
20942 } else {
20943 return last_value;
20944 }
20945 }
20946 };
20947
20955 struct reflection_init {
20956 template <U Value>
20957 static U handle_constant(U last_value, This& me) {
20958 if constexpr (enum_constant_is_valid_wrap<E, Value>()) {
20959 // Constant is valid, so fill the reflection data.
20960 auto v = Value;
20961 const char *name = enum_constant_to_name<E, flecs_enum_cast(E, Value)>();
20962
20963 ++me.max; // Increment cursor as we build the constants array.
20964
20965 // If the enum was previously contiguous, and continues to be
20966 // through the current value...
20967 if (me.has_contiguous && static_cast<U>(me.max) == v && me.contiguous_until == v) {
20968 ++me.contiguous_until;
20969 }
20970
20971 // else, if the enum was never contiguous and hasn't been set as not
20972 // contiguous...
20973 else if (!me.contiguous_until && me.has_contiguous) {
20974 me.has_contiguous = false;
20975 }
20976
20977 ecs_assert(!(last_value > 0 &&
20978 v < std::numeric_limits<U>::min() + last_value),
20979 ECS_UNSUPPORTED,
20980 "Signed integer enums cause integer overflow when recording "
20981 "offset from high positive to low negative. Consider using "
20982 "unsigned integers as the underlying type.");
20983
20984 me.constants[me.max].value = v;
20985 me.constants[me.max].offset = v - last_value;
20986 me.constants[me.max].name = name;
20987 if (!me.constants[me.max].index) {
20988 me.constants[me.max].index =
20989 flecs_component_ids_index_get();
20990 }
20991
20992 return v;
20993 } else {
20994 // Search for the constant failed. Pass the last valid value through.
20995 return last_value;
20996 }
20997 }
20998 };
20999public:
21000
21002 enum_type() {
21003 // Initialize/reset reflection data values to the default state.
21004 min = 0;
21005 max = -1;
21006 has_contiguous = true;
21007 contiguous_until = 0;
21008
21009#if FLECS_CPP_ENUM_REFLECTION_SUPPORT
21010 enum_reflection<E, reflection_init>::
21011 template each_enum< static_cast<U>(enum_last<E>::value) >(*this);
21012#endif
21013 }
21014
21016 static enum_type<E>& get() {
21017 static _::enum_type<E> instance;
21018 return instance;
21019 }
21020
21022 flecs::entity_t entity(E value) const {
21023 int index = index_by_value(value);
21024 if (index >= 0) {
21025 return constants[index].id;
21026 }
21027 return 0;
21028 }
21029
21031 void register_for_world(flecs::world_t *world, flecs::entity_t id) {
21032#if !FLECS_CPP_ENUM_REFLECTION_SUPPORT
21033 ecs_abort(ECS_UNSUPPORTED, "enum reflection requires gcc 7.5 or higher")
21034#endif
21035
21036 ecs_log_push();
21037 ecs_cpp_enum_init(world, id, type<U>::id(world));
21038
21039 for (U v = 0; v < static_cast<U>(max + 1); v ++) {
21040 if (constants[v].index) {
21041 flecs::entity_t constant = ecs_cpp_enum_constant_register(world,
21042 type<E>::id(world), 0, constants[v].name, &constants[v].value,
21043 type<U>::id(world), sizeof(U));
21044
21045 flecs_component_ids_set(world, constants[v].index, constant);
21046 }
21047 }
21048
21049 ecs_log_pop();
21050 }
21051
21052 int min;
21053 int max;
21054
21055 // If enum constants start non-sparse, contiguous_until will be the index of
21056 // the first sparse value, or the end of the constants array.
21057 U contiguous_until;
21058
21059 // Compile-time-generated count of enum constants.
21060 static constexpr unsigned int constants_size =
21061 enum_reflection<E, reflection_count>::
21062 template each_enum< static_cast<U>(enum_last<E>::value) >();
21063
21064 // Constants array is sized to the number of found constants, or 1
21065 // to avoid a zero-sized array.
21066 #ifdef FLECS_CPP_ENUM_REFLECTION
21067 enum_constant<U> constants[constants_size? constants_size: 1] = {};
21068 bool has_contiguous;
21069 #else
21070 // If we're not using enum reflection, we cannot statically determine the
21071 // upper bound of the enum, so use 128.
21072 enum_constant<U> constants[128] = {};
21073 bool has_contiguous = true; // Assume contiguous IDs.
21074 #endif
21075};
21076
21078template <typename E>
21079inline static void init_enum(flecs::world_t *world, flecs::entity_t id) {
21080 (void)world; (void)id;
21081 if constexpr (is_enum_v<E>) {
21082 _::enum_type<E>::get().register_for_world(world, id);
21083 }
21084}
21085
21086} // namespace _
21087
21089template <typename E>
21090struct enum_data {
21091 using U = underlying_type_t<E>;
21092
21094 enum_data(flecs::world_t *world, _::enum_type<E>& impl)
21095 : world_(world)
21096 , impl_(impl) { }
21097
21105 bool is_valid(U value) {
21106 int index = index_by_value(value);
21107 if (index < 0) {
21108 return false;
21109 }
21110 return impl_.constants[index].index != 0;
21111 }
21112
21120 bool is_valid(E value) {
21121 return is_valid(static_cast<U>(value));
21122 }
21123
21130 int index_by_value(U value) const {
21131 if (impl_.max < 0) {
21132 return -1;
21133 }
21134
21135 // Check if value is in the contiguous lookup section.
21136 if (impl_.has_contiguous && value < impl_.contiguous_until && value >= 0) {
21137 return static_cast<int>(value);
21138 }
21139 U accumulator = impl_.contiguous_until? impl_.contiguous_until - 1: 0;
21140 for (int i = static_cast<int>(impl_.contiguous_until); i <= impl_.max; ++i) {
21141 accumulator += impl_.constants[i].offset;
21142 if (accumulator == value) {
21143 return i;
21144 }
21145 }
21146 return -1;
21147 }
21148
21155 int index_by_value(E value) const {
21156 return index_by_value(static_cast<U>(value));
21157 }
21158
21160 int first() const {
21161 return impl_.min;
21162 }
21163
21165 int last() const {
21166 return impl_.max;
21167 }
21168
21170 int next(int cur) const {
21171 return cur + 1;
21172 }
21173
21175 flecs::entity entity() const;
21177 flecs::entity entity(U value) const;
21179 flecs::entity entity(E value) const;
21180
21187 #ifdef FLECS_CPP_NO_ENUM_REFLECTION
21188 void register_constant(flecs::world_t *world, U v, flecs::entity_t e) {
21189 if (v < 128) {
21190 if (!impl_.constants[v].index) {
21191 impl_.constants[v].index = flecs_component_ids_index_get();
21192 }
21193
21194 flecs_component_ids_set(world, impl_.constants[v].index, e);
21195
21196 impl_.max ++;
21197
21198 if (impl_.contiguous_until <= v) {
21199 impl_.contiguous_until = v + 1;
21200 }
21201 }
21202 }
21203 #endif
21204
21205 flecs::world_t *world_;
21206 _::enum_type<E>& impl_;
21207};
21208
21210template <typename E>
21211enum_data<E> enum_type(flecs::world_t *world) {
21212 _::type<E>::id(world); // Ensure the enum is registered.
21213 auto& ref = _::enum_type<E>::get();
21214 return enum_data<E>(world, ref);
21215}

21217} // namespace flecs

21472template <typename K, typename V>
21473struct map_entry {
21474 K first;
21475 V second;
21476};
21477
21478template <typename K, typename V>
21479struct map_iterator {
21480 map_iterator()
21481 : map_(nullptr)
21482 , done_(true) { }
21483
21484 explicit map_iterator(const ecs_map_t *m)
21485 : map_(m)
21486 {
21487 if (m) {
21488 it_ = ecs_map_iter(m);
21489 advance();
21490 } else {
21491 done_ = true;
21492 }
21493 }
21494
21495 bool operator!=(const map_iterator& other) const {
21496 return done_ != other.done_;
21497 }
21498
21499 const map_entry<K, V>& operator*() const {
21500 return entry_;
21501 }
21502
21503 const map_entry<K, V>* operator->() const {
21504 return &entry_;
21505 }
21506
21507 map_iterator& operator++() {
21508 advance();
21509 return *this;
21510 }
21511
21512private:
21513 void advance() {
21514 if (ecs_map_next(&it_)) {
21515 entry_.first = static_cast<K>(ecs_map_key(&it_));
21516 entry_.second = _::map_value_cast<V>(ecs_map_value(&it_));
21517 done_ = false;
21518 } else {
21519 done_ = true;
21520 }
21521 }
21522
21523 const ecs_map_t *map_;
21524 ecs_map_iter_t it_ = {};
21525 map_entry<K, V> entry_ = {};
21526 bool done_ = false;
21527};
21528
21529template <typename K, typename V>
21530struct map {
21531 explicit map(const ecs_map_t *m) : map_(m) { }
21532
21533 map_iterator<K, V> begin() const {
21534 return map_iterator<K, V>(map_);
21535 }
21536
21537 map_iterator<K, V> end() const {
21538 return map_iterator<K, V>();
21539 }
21540
21541private:
21542 const ecs_map_t *map_;
21543};
21544

21753template <typename Base, typename E>
21754struct event_builder_base {
21755 event_builder_base(flecs::world_t *world, flecs::entity_t event)
21756 : world_(world)
21757 , desc_{}
21758 , ids_{}
21759 , ids_array_{}
21760 {
21761 desc_.event = event;
21762 }
21763
21765 template <typename T>
21766 Base& id() {
21767 ids_.array = ids_array_;
21768 ids_.array[ids_.count] = _::type<T>().id(world_);
21769 ids_.count ++;
21770 return *this;
21771 }
21772
21778 template <typename First, typename Second>
21779 Base& id() {
21780 return id(
21781 ecs_pair(_::type<First>::id(this->world_),
21782 _::type<Second>::id(this->world_)));
21783 }
21784
21790 template <typename First>
21791 Base& id(entity_t second) {
21792 return id(ecs_pair(_::type<First>::id(this->world_), second));
21793 }
21794
21800 Base& id(entity_t first, entity_t second) {
21801 return id(ecs_pair(first, second));
21802 }
21803
21809 template <typename Enum, if_t<is_enum<Enum>::value> = 0>
21810 Base& id(Enum value) {
21811 const auto& et = enum_type<Enum>(this->world_);
21812 flecs::entity_t target = et.entity(value);
21813 return id(et.entity(), target);
21814 }
21815
21817 Base& id(flecs::id_t id) {
21818 ids_.array = ids_array_;
21819 ids_.array[ids_.count] = id;
21820 ids_.count ++;
21821 return *this;
21822 }
21823
21825 Base& entity(flecs::entity_t e) {
21826 desc_.entity = e;
21827 return *this;
21828 }
21829
21831 Base& table(flecs::table_t *t, int32_t offset = 0, int32_t count = 0) {
21832 desc_.table = t;
21833 desc_.offset = offset;
21834 desc_.count = count;
21835 return *this;
21836 }
21837
21839 Base& ctx(const E* ptr) {
21840 desc_.const_param = ptr;
21841 return *this;
21842 }
21843
21845 Base& ctx(E* ptr) {
21846 desc_.param = ptr;
21847 return *this;
21848 }
21849
21851 void emit() {
21852 ids_.array = ids_array_;
21853 desc_.ids = &ids_;
21854 desc_.observable = const_cast<flecs::world_t*>(ecs_get_world(world_));
21855 ecs_emit(world_, &desc_);
21856 }
21857
21859 void enqueue() {
21860 ids_.array = ids_array_;
21861 desc_.ids = &ids_;
21862 desc_.observable = const_cast<flecs::world_t*>(ecs_get_world(world_));
21863 ecs_enqueue(world_, &desc_);
21864 }
21865
21866protected:
21867 flecs::world_t *world_;
21868 ecs_event_desc_t desc_;
21869 flecs::type_t ids_;
21870 flecs::id_t ids_array_[ECS_EVENT_DESC_ID_COUNT_MAX];
21871
21872private:
21873 operator Base&() {
21874 return *static_cast<Base*>(this);
21875 }
21876};

23437
23439 int run() {
23440 int result = ecs_app_run(world_, &desc_);
23441 if (ecs_should_quit(world_)) {
23442 // Only free world if quit flag is set. This ensures that we won't
23443 // try to clean up the world if the app is used in an environment
23444 // that takes over the main loop, like with emscripten.
23445 if (!flecs_poly_release(world_)) {
23446 ecs_fini(world_);
23447 }
23448 }
23449 return result;
23450 }
23451
23452private:
23453 flecs::world_t *world_;
23454 ecs_app_desc_t desc_;
23455};
23456
23459}

23837// T()
23838// Can't coexist with T(flecs::entity) or T(flecs::world, flecs::entity).
23839template <typename T>
23840void ctor_impl(void *ptr, int32_t count, const ecs_type_info_t *info) {
23841 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23842 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23843 T *arr = static_cast<T*>(ptr);
23844 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23845 FLECS_PLACEMENT_NEW(&arr[i], T);
23846 }
23847}
23848
23849// ~T()
23850template <typename T>
23851void dtor_impl(void *ptr, int32_t count, const ecs_type_info_t *info) {
23852 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23853 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23854 T *arr = static_cast<T*>(ptr);
23855 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23856 arr[i].~T();
23857 }
23858}

23860// T& operator=(const T&)
23861template <typename T>
23862void copy_impl(void *dst_ptr, const void *src_ptr, int32_t count,
23863 const ecs_type_info_t *info)
23864{
23865 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23866 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23867 T *dst_arr = static_cast<T*>(dst_ptr);
23868 const T *src_arr = static_cast<const T*>(src_ptr);
23869 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23870 dst_arr[i] = src_arr[i];
23871 }
23872}

23874// T& operator=(T&&)
23875template <typename T>
23876void move_impl(void *dst_ptr, void *src_ptr, int32_t count,
23877 const ecs_type_info_t *info)
23878{
23879 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23880 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23881 T *dst_arr = static_cast<T*>(dst_ptr);
23882 T *src_arr = static_cast<T*>(src_ptr);
23883 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23884 dst_arr[i] = FLECS_MOV(src_arr[i]);
23885 }

23889template <typename T>
23890void copy_ctor_impl(void *dst_ptr, const void *src_ptr, int32_t count,
23891 const ecs_type_info_t *info)
23892{
23893 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),

23903template <typename T>
23904void move_ctor_impl(void *dst_ptr, void *src_ptr, int32_t count,
23905 const ecs_type_info_t *info)
23906{
23907 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23908 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23909 T *dst_arr = static_cast<T*>(dst_ptr);
23910 T *src_arr = static_cast<T*>(src_ptr);
23911 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23912 FLECS_PLACEMENT_NEW(&dst_arr[i], T(FLECS_MOV(src_arr[i])));
23913 }

23916// T(T&&), ~T()
23917// Typically used when moving to a new table, and removing from the old table.
23918template <typename T>
23919void ctor_move_dtor_impl(void *dst_ptr, void *src_ptr, int32_t count,
23920 const ecs_type_info_t *info)
23921{
23922 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23923 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23924 T *dst_arr = static_cast<T*>(dst_ptr);
23925 T *src_arr = static_cast<T*>(src_ptr);
23926 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23927 FLECS_PLACEMENT_NEW(&dst_arr[i], T(FLECS_MOV(src_arr[i])));
23928 src_arr[i].~T();
23929 }
23930}

23932// Move assign + dtor (non-trivial move assignment).
23933// Typically used when moving a component to a deleted component.
23934template <typename T, if_not_t<
23935 std::is_trivially_move_assignable<T>::value > = 0>
23936void move_dtor_impl(void *dst_ptr, void *src_ptr, int32_t count,
23937 const ecs_type_info_t *info)
23938{
23939 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23940 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23941 T *dst_arr = static_cast<T*>(dst_ptr);
23942 T *src_arr = static_cast<T*>(src_ptr);
23943 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23944 // Move assignment should free dst and assign dst to src.
23945 dst_arr[i] = FLECS_MOV(src_arr[i]);
23946 // Destruct src. Move should have left the object in a state where it no
23947 // longer holds resources, but it still needs to be destructed.
23948 src_arr[i].~T();
23949 }
23950}
23951
23952// Move assign + dtor (trivial move assignment).
23953// Typically used when moving a component to a deleted component.
23954template <typename T, if_t<
23955 std::is_trivially_move_assignable<T>::value > = 0>
23956void move_dtor_impl(void *dst_ptr, void *src_ptr, int32_t count,
23957 const ecs_type_info_t *info)
23958{
23959 (void)info; ecs_assert(info->size == ECS_SIZEOF(T),
23960 ECS_INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL);
23961 T *dst_arr = static_cast<T*>(dst_ptr);
23962 T *src_arr = static_cast<T*>(src_ptr);
23963 for (int i = 0; i < count; i ++) {
23964 // Clean up resources of dst.
23965 dst_arr[i].~T();
23966 // Copy src to dst.
23967 dst_arr[i] = FLECS_MOV(src_arr[i]);
23968 // No need to destruct src. Since this is a trivial move, the code
23969 // should be agnostic to the address of the component, which means we
23970 // can pretend nothing got destructed.
23971 }
23972}

23989 return nullptr;

23991 flags |= ECS_TYPE_HOOK_CTOR_ILLEGAL;

24003 flecs_static_assert(always_false<T>::value,
24004 "component type must be destructible");
24005 flags |= ECS_TYPE_HOOK_DTOR_ILLEGAL;
24006 return nullptr;
24007 } else {

24084// Traits to check for operator<, operator>, and operator==.
24085using std::void_t;
24086
24087// These traits cause a "float comparison warning" in some compilers
24088// when `T` is float or double.
24089// Disable this warning with the following pragmas.
24090#if defined(__clang__)
24091 #pragma clang diagnostic push
24092 #pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wfloat-equal"
24093#elif defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__)
24094 #pragma GCC diagnostic push
24095 #pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wfloat-equal"
24096#endif
24097
24098// Trait to check for operator<.
24099template <typename T, typename = void>
24100struct has_operator_less : std::false_type {};
24101
24102// Only enable if T has an operator< that takes T as the right-hand side (no implicit conversion).
24103template <typename T>
24104struct has_operator_less<T, void_t<decltype(std::declval<const T&>() < std::declval<const T&>())>> :
24105 std::is_same<decltype(std::declval<const T&>() < std::declval<const T&>()), bool> {};
24106
24107// Trait to check for operator>.
24108template <typename T, typename = void>
24109struct has_operator_greater : std::false_type {};
24110
24111// Only enable if T has an operator> that takes T as the right-hand side (no implicit conversion).
24112template <typename T>
24113struct has_operator_greater<T, void_t<decltype(std::declval<const T&>() > std::declval<const T&>())>> :
24114 std::is_same<decltype(std::declval<const T&>() > std::declval<const T&>()), bool> {};
24115
24116// Trait to check for operator==.
24117template <typename T, typename = void>
24118struct has_operator_equal : std::false_type {};
24119
24120// Only enable if T has an operator== that takes T as the right-hand side (no implicit conversion).
24121template <typename T>
24122struct has_operator_equal<T, void_t<decltype(std::declval<const T&>() == std::declval<const T&>())>> :
24123 std::is_same<decltype(std::declval<const T&>() == std::declval<const T&>()), bool> {};
24124
24125// Selects the best comparison strategy based on available operators.
24126template <typename T>
24127int compare_impl(const void *a, const void *b, const ecs_type_info_t *) {
24128 const T& lhs = *static_cast<const T*>(a);
24129 const T& rhs = *static_cast<const T*>(b);
24130
24131 if constexpr (has_operator_less<T>::value && has_operator_equal<T>::value) {
24132 // 2. Compare function if `<` and `==` are defined (preferred)
24133 if (lhs == rhs) return 0;
24134 if (lhs < rhs) return -1;
24135 return 1;
24136 } else if constexpr (has_operator_greater<T>::value && has_operator_equal<T>::value) {
24137 // 3. Compare function if `>` and `==` are defined, deducing `<`
24138 if (lhs == rhs) return 0;
24139 if (lhs > rhs) return 1;
24140 return -1;
24141 } else if constexpr (has_operator_less<T>::value && has_operator_greater<T>::value) {
24142 // 1. Compare function if `<`, `>` are defined
24143 if (lhs < rhs) return -1;
24144 if (lhs > rhs) return 1;
24145 return 0;
24146 } else if constexpr (has_operator_less<T>::value) {
24147 // 4. Compare function if only `<` is defined
24148 if (lhs < rhs) return -1;
24149 if (rhs < lhs) return 1;
24150 return 0;
24151 } else if constexpr (has_operator_greater<T>::value) {
24152 // 5. Compare function if only `>` is defined
24153 if (lhs > rhs) return 1;
24154 if (rhs > lhs) return -1;
24155 return 0;
24156 } else {
24157 // This branch should never be instantiated due to the compare() check.
24158 return 0;
24159 }
24160}
24161
24162// To have a generated compare hook, at least
24163// operator> or operator< must be defined.
24164template <typename T>
24165ecs_cmp_t compare() {
24166 if constexpr (has_operator_less<T>::value || has_operator_greater<T>::value) {
24167 return compare_impl<T>;
24168 } else {
24169 return NULL;
24170 }
24171}
24172
24173// Equals implementation.
24174template <typename T>
24175bool equals_impl(const void *a, const void *b, const ecs_type_info_t *) {
24176 const T& lhs = *static_cast<const T*>(a);
24177 const T& rhs = *static_cast<const T*>(b);
24178 return lhs == rhs;
24179}
24180
24181template <typename T>
24182ecs_equals_t equals() {
24183 if constexpr (has_operator_equal<T>::value) {
24184 return equals_impl<T>;
24185 } else {
24186 return NULL;
24187 }
24188}
24189
24190// Re-enable the float comparison warning.
24191#if defined(__clang__)
24192 #pragma clang diagnostic pop
24193#elif defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__)
24194 #pragma GCC diagnostic pop
24195#endif
24196
24197} // namespace _
24198} // namespace flecs

24215template <typename T>
24216inline void set(world_t *world, flecs::entity_t entity, T&& value, flecs::id_t id) {
24217 ecs_assert(_::type<T>::size() != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
24218 "operation invalid for empty type");
24219
24220 ecs_cpp_get_mut_t res = ecs_cpp_set(world, entity, id, &value, sizeof(T));
24221
24222 T& dst = *static_cast<remove_reference_t<T>*>(res.ptr);
24223 if constexpr (std::is_copy_assignable_v<T>) {
24224 dst = FLECS_FWD(value);
24225 } else {
24226 dst = FLECS_MOV(value);
24227 }
24228
24229 if (res.stage) {
24230 flecs_defer_end(res.world, res.stage);
24231 }
24232
24233 if (res.call_modified) {
24234 ecs_modified_id(world, entity, id);
24235 }
24236}
24237
24246template <typename T>
24247inline void set(world_t *world, flecs::entity_t entity, const T& value, flecs::id_t id) {
24248 ecs_assert(_::type<T>::size() != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
24249 "operation invalid for empty type");
24250
24251 ecs_cpp_get_mut_t res = ecs_cpp_set(world, entity, id, &value, sizeof(T));
24252
24253 T& dst = *static_cast<remove_reference_t<T>*>(res.ptr);
24254 dst = value;
24255
24256 if (res.stage) {
24257 flecs_defer_end(res.world, res.stage);
24258 }
24259
24260 if (res.call_modified) {
24261 ecs_modified_id(world, entity, id);
24262 }
24263}

24302template <typename T>
24303inline void assign(world_t *world, flecs::entity_t entity, T&& value, flecs::id_t id) {
24304 ecs_assert(_::type<remove_reference_t<T>>::size() != 0,
24305 ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER, "operation invalid for empty type");
24306
24307 ecs_cpp_get_mut_t res = ecs_cpp_assign(
24308 world, entity, id, &value, sizeof(T));
24309
24310 T& dst = *static_cast<remove_reference_t<T>*>(res.ptr);
24311 if constexpr (std::is_copy_assignable_v<T>) {
24312 dst = FLECS_FWD(value);
24313 } else {
24314 dst = FLECS_MOV(value);
24315 }
24316
24317 if (res.stage) {
24318 flecs_defer_end(res.world, res.stage);
24319 }
24320
24321 if (res.call_modified) {
24322 ecs_modified_id(world, entity, id);
24323 }
24324}
24325
24335template <typename T>
24336inline void assign(world_t *world, flecs::entity_t entity, const T& value, flecs::id_t id) {
24337 ecs_assert(_::type<remove_reference_t<T>>::size() != 0,
24338 ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER, "operation invalid for empty type");
24339
24340 ecs_cpp_get_mut_t res = ecs_cpp_assign(
24341 world, entity, id, &value, sizeof(T));
24342
24343 T& dst = *static_cast<remove_reference_t<T>*>(res.ptr);
24344 dst = value;
24345
24346 if (res.stage) {
24347 flecs_defer_end(res.world, res.stage);
24348 }
24349
24350 if (res.call_modified) {
24351 ecs_modified_id(world, entity, id);
24352 }
24353}

24392template <typename T, typename ... Args, if_t<
24393 std::is_constructible<actual_type_t<T>, Args...>::value ||
24394 std::is_default_constructible<actual_type_t<T>>::value > = 0>
24395inline void emplace(world_t *world, flecs::entity_t entity, flecs::id_t id, Args&&... args) {
24396 ecs_assert(_::type<T>::size() != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
24397 "operation invalid for empty type");
24398 T& dst = *static_cast<T*>(ecs_emplace_id(world, entity, id, sizeof(T), nullptr));
24399
24400 FLECS_PLACEMENT_NEW(&dst, T{FLECS_FWD(args)...});
24401
24402 ecs_modified_id(world, entity, id);
24403}

24439struct world {
24442 explicit world()
24443 : world_( ecs_init() ) {
24444 init_builtin_components();
24445 }
24446
24451 explicit world(int argc, char *argv[])
24452 : world_( ecs_init_w_args(argc, argv) ) {
24453 init_builtin_components();
24454 }
24455
24458 explicit world(world_t *w)
24459 : world_( w ) {
24460 if (w) {
24461 flecs_poly_claim(w);
24462 }
24463 }
24464
24467 world(const world& obj) {
24468 this->world_ = obj.world_;
24469 flecs_poly_claim(this->world_);
24470 }
24471
24473 world& operator=(const world& obj) noexcept {
24474 release();
24475 this->world_ = obj.world_;
24476 flecs_poly_claim(this->world_);
24477 return *this;
24478 }
24479
24481 world(world&& obj) noexcept {
24482 world_ = obj.world_;
24483 obj.world_ = nullptr;
24484 }
24485
24487 world& operator=(world&& obj) noexcept {
24488 release();
24489 world_ = obj.world_;
24490 obj.world_ = nullptr;
24491 return *this;
24492 }
24493
24497 void release() {
24498 if (world_) {
24499 if (!flecs_poly_release(world_)) {
24500 if (ecs_stage_get_id(world_) == -1) {
24501 ecs_stage_free(world_);
24502 } else {
24503 // Before we call ecs_fini(), we increment the reference count back to 1.
24504 // Otherwise, copies of this object created during ecs_fini() (e.g., a component on_remove hook)
24505 // would again call this destructor and ecs_fini().
24506 flecs_poly_claim(world_);
24507 ecs_fini(world_);
24508 }
24509 }
24510 world_ = nullptr;
24511 }
24512 }
24513
24515 ~world() {
24516 release();
24517 }

24520 operator world_t*() const { return world_; }

24529 void make_owner() {
24530 flecs_poly_release(world_);

24534 void reset() {
24535 /* Make sure there's only one reference to the world. */
24536 ecs_assert(flecs_poly_refcount(world_) == 1, ECS_INVALID_OPERATION,
24537 "reset would invalidate other handles");
24538 ecs_fini(world_);
24539 world_ = ecs_init();
24540 init_builtin_components();
24541 }

26426struct untyped_field {
26427 untyped_field(void* array, size_t size, size_t count, bool is_shared = false)
26428 : data_(array)
26429 , size_(size)
26430 , count_(count)
26431 , is_shared_(is_shared) {}
26432
26439 void* operator[](size_t index) const {
26440 ecs_assert(!is_shared_ || !index, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
26441 "invalid usage of [] operator for shared component field");
26442 ecs_assert(index < count_, ECS_COLUMN_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE,
26443 "index %d out of range for field", index);
26444 return ECS_OFFSET(data_, size_ * index);
26445 }
26446
26447protected:
26448 void* data_;
26449 size_t size_;
26450 size_t count_;
26451 bool is_shared_;
26452};

26475

26482
26489 T& operator[](size_t index) const;
26490
26496 T& operator*() const;
26497
26503 T* operator->() const;
26504
26505protected:
26506 T* data_;
26507 size_t count_;
26508 bool is_shared_;
26509};

26538template <typename T>
26539struct range_iterator
26540{
26541 explicit range_iterator(T value)
26542 : value_(value){}
26543
26544 bool operator!=(range_iterator const& other) const
26545 {
26546 return value_ != other.value_;
26547 }
26548
26549 T const& operator*() const
26550 {
26551 return value_;
26552 }
26553
26554 range_iterator& operator++()
26555 {
26556 ++value_;
26557 return *this;
26558 }
26559
26560private:
26561 T value_;
26562};

26992private:
26993 /* Get field, check if correct type is used. */
26994 template <typename T, typename A = actual_type_t<T>>
26995 flecs::field<T> get_field(int8_t index) const {
26996
26997#ifndef FLECS_NDEBUG
26998 ecs_entity_t term_id = ecs_field_id(iter_, index);
26999 ecs_assert(ECS_HAS_ID_FLAG(term_id, PAIR) ||
27000 term_id == _::type<T>::id(iter_->world),
27001 ECS_COLUMN_TYPE_MISMATCH, NULL);
27002#endif
27003
27004 size_t count;
27005 bool is_shared = !ecs_field_is_self(iter_, index);
27006
27007 /* If a shared field is retrieved with field(), there will only be a
27008 * single value. Ensure that the application does not accidentally read
27009 * out of bounds. */
27010 if (is_shared) {
27011 count = 1;
27012 } else {
27013 /* If field is owned, there will be as many values as there are
27014 * entities. */
27015 count = static_cast<size_t>(iter_->count);
27016 }
27017
27018 return flecs::field<A>(
27019 static_cast<T*>(ecs_field_w_size(iter_, sizeof(A), index)),
27020 count, is_shared);
27021 }
27022
27023 /* Get field, check if correct type is used. */
27024 template <typename T, typename A = actual_type_t<T>>
27025 flecs::field<T> get_field_at(int8_t index, int32_t row) const {
27026
27027#ifndef FLECS_NDEBUG
27028 ecs_entity_t term_id = ecs_field_id(iter_, index);
27029 ecs_assert(ECS_HAS_ID_FLAG(term_id, PAIR) ||
27030 term_id == _::type<T>::id(iter_->world),
27031 ECS_COLUMN_TYPE_MISMATCH, NULL);
27032#endif
27033
27034 return flecs::field<A>(
27035 static_cast<T*>(ecs_field_at_w_size(iter_, sizeof(A), index, row)),
27036 1, false);
27037 }
27038
27039 flecs::untyped_field get_unchecked_field(int8_t index) const {
27040 size_t count;
27041 size_t size = ecs_field_size(iter_, index);
27042 bool is_shared = !ecs_field_is_self(iter_, index);
27043
27044 /* If a shared field is retrieved with field(), there will only be a
27045 * single value. Ensure that the application does not accidentally read
27046 * out of bounds. */
27047 if (is_shared) {
27048 count = 1;
27049 } else {
27050 /* If field is owned, there will be as many values as there are
27051 * entities. */
27052 count = static_cast<size_t>(iter_->count);
27053 }
27054
27055 return flecs::untyped_field(
27056 ecs_field_w_size(iter_, size, index), size, count, is_shared);
27057 }
27058
27059 flecs::untyped_field get_unchecked_field_at(int8_t index, size_t row) const {
27060 size_t size = ecs_field_size(iter_, index);
27061 return flecs::untyped_field(
27062 ecs_field_at_w_size(iter_, size, index, static_cast<int32_t>(row)),
27063 size, 1, false);
27064 }
27065
27066 flecs::iter_t *iter_;
27067};

27089struct untyped_ref {
27090
27092 untyped_ref () : world_(nullptr), ref_{}, id_(0) {}
27093
27100 untyped_ref(world_t *world, entity_t entity, flecs::id_t id)
27101 : ref_(), id_(id) {
27102 ecs_assert(id != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
27103 "invalid id");
27104 // The world we were called with may be a stage; convert it to a world
27105 // here if that is the case.
27106 world_ = world ? const_cast<flecs::world_t *>(ecs_get_world(world))
27107 : nullptr;
27108
27109#ifdef FLECS_DEBUG
27110 flecs::entity_t type = ecs_get_typeid(world, id);
27111 const flecs::type_info_t *ti = ecs_get_type_info(world, type);
27112 ecs_assert(ti && ti->size != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
27113 "cannot create ref to empty type");
27114#endif
27115 ref_ = ecs_ref_init_id(world_, entity, id);
27116 }
27117
27123 untyped_ref(flecs::entity entity, flecs::id_t id);
27124
27126 flecs::entity entity() const;
27127
27129 flecs::id component() const {
27130 return flecs::id(world_, id_);
27131 }
27132
27134 void* get() {
27135 return ecs_ref_get_id(world_, &ref_, id_);
27136 }
27137
27139 bool has() {
27140 return !!try_get();
27141 }
27142
27144 flecs::world world() const {
27145 return flecs::world(world_);
27146 }
27147
27151 operator bool() {
27152 return has();
27153 }
27154
27158 void* try_get() {
27159 if (!world_ || !ref_.entity) {
27160 return nullptr;
27161 }
27162
27163 return get();
27164 }
27165
27166private:
27167 world_t *world_;
27168 flecs::ref_t ref_;
27169 flecs::id_t id_;
27170};
27171
27175template <typename T>
27176struct ref : public untyped_ref {
27178 ref() : untyped_ref() { }
27179
27186 ref(world_t *world, entity_t entity, flecs::id_t id = 0)
27187 : untyped_ref(world, entity, id ? id : _::type<T>::id(world))
27188 { }
27189
27195 ref(flecs::entity entity, flecs::id_t id = 0);
27196
27198 T* operator->() {
27199 T* result = static_cast<T*>(get());
27200
27201 ecs_assert(result != NULL, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
27202 "nullptr dereference by flecs::ref");
27203
27204 return result;
27205 }
27206
27208 T* get() {
27209 return static_cast<T*>(untyped_ref::get());
27210 }
27211
27215 T* try_get() {
27216 return static_cast<T*>(untyped_ref::try_get());
27217 }
27218};

27593 template <typename Func>
27594 void children(flecs::entity_t rel, Func&& func) const {
27595 /* When the entity is a wildcard, this would attempt to query for all
27596 * entities with (ChildOf, *) or (ChildOf, _) instead of querying for
27597 * the children of the wildcard entity. */
27598 if (id_ == flecs::Wildcard || id_ == flecs::Any) {
27599 /* This is correct, wildcard entities don't have children. */
27600 return;
27601 }
27602
27603 flecs::world world(world_);
27604
27605 ecs_iter_t it = ecs_children_w_rel(world_, rel, id_);
27606 while (ecs_children_next(&it)) {
27607 _::each_delegate<Func>(FLECS_MOV(func)).invoke(&it);
27608 }
27609 }
27610
27621 template <typename Rel, typename Func>
27622 void children(Func&& func) const {
27623 children(_::type<Rel>::id(world_), FLECS_MOV(func));
27624 }
27625
27637 template <typename Func>
27638 void children(Func&& func) const {
27639 children(flecs::ChildOf, FLECS_MOV(func));
27640 }

27642 /* try_get */
27643
27650 template <typename T, if_t< is_actual<T>::value > = 0>
27651 const T* try_get() const {
27652 auto comp_id = _::type<T>::id(world_);
27653 ecs_assert(_::type<T>::size() != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
27654 "operation invalid for empty type");
27655 return static_cast<const T*>(ecs_get_id(world_, id_, comp_id));
27656 }
27657
27666 template <typename T, typename A = actual_type_t<T>,
27667 if_t< flecs::is_pair<T>::value > = 0>
27668 const A* try_get() const {
27669 auto comp_id = _::type<T>::id(world_);
27670 ecs_assert(_::type<A>::size() != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
27671 "operation invalid for empty type");
27672 return static_cast<const A*>(ecs_get_id(world_, id_, comp_id));
27673 }
27674
27682 template <typename First, typename Second, typename P = pair<First, Second>,
27683 typename A = actual_type_t<P>, if_not_t< flecs::is_pair<First>::value > = 0>
27684 const A* try_get() const {
27685 return this->try_get<P>();
27686 }
27687
27695 template<typename First, typename Second, if_not_t< is_enum<Second>::value> = 0>
27696 const First* try_get(Second second) const {
27697 auto first = _::type<First>::id(world_);
27698 ecs_assert(_::type<First>::size() != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
27699 "operation invalid for empty type");
27700 return static_cast<const First*>(
27701 ecs_get_id(world_, id_, ecs_pair(first, second)));
27702 }
27703
27711 template<typename First, typename Second, if_t< is_enum<Second>::value && !std::is_same<First, Second>::value > = 0>
27712 const First* try_get(Second constant) const {
27713 const auto& et = enum_type<Second>(this->world_);
27714 flecs::entity_t target = et.entity(constant);
27715 return try_get<First>(target);
27716 }
27717
27724 const void* try_get(flecs::id_t comp) const {
27725 return ecs_get_id(world_, id_, comp);
27726 }
27727
27737 const void* try_get(flecs::entity_t first, flecs::entity_t second) const {
27738 return ecs_get_id(world_, id_, ecs_pair(first, second));
27739 }

27746 template<typename... Ts>
27747 auto try_get_n() const {
27748 flecs_static_assert(sizeof...(Ts) > 1, "try_get_n requires at least two components");
27749 flecs_static_assert(sizeof...(Ts) < 9, "try_get_n cannot fetch more than eight components");
27750 return typename tuple_builder<sizeof...(Ts), Ts...>::type_const_ptr {try_get<Ts>()...};
27751 }
27752
27761 template<typename Second>
27762 const Second* try_get_second(flecs::entity_t first) const {
27763 auto second = _::type<Second>::id(world_);
27764 ecs_assert( ecs_get_type_info(world_, ecs_pair(first, second)) != NULL,
27765 ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER, "pair is not a component");
27766 ecs_assert( ecs_get_type_info(world_, ecs_pair(first, second))->component == second,
27767 ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER, "type of pair is not Second");
27768 ecs_assert(_::type<Second>::size() != 0, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
27769 "operation invalid for empty type");
27770 return static_cast<const Second*>(
27771 ecs_get_id(world_, id_, ecs_pair(first, second)));
27772 }
27773
27782 template<typename First, typename Second>
27783 const Second* try_get_second() const {
27784 return try_get<pair_object<First, Second>>();
27785 }

28403 template <typename T>
28404 bool has() const {
28405 flecs::id_t cid = _::type<T>::id(world_);
28406 bool result = ecs_has_id(world_, id_, cid);
28407 if (result) {
28408 return result;
28409 }
28410
28411 if (is_enum<T>::value) {
28412 return ecs_has_pair(world_, id_, cid, flecs::Wildcard);
28413 }
28414
28415 return false;
28416 }

28424 template <typename E, if_t< is_enum<E>::value > = 0>
28425 bool has(E value) const {
28426 auto r = _::type<E>::id(world_);
28427 auto o = enum_type<E>(world_).entity(value);
28428 ecs_assert(o, ECS_INVALID_PARAMETER,
28429 "Constant was not found in Enum reflection data."
28430 " Did you mean to use has<E>() instead of has(E)?");
28431 return ecs_has_pair(world_, id_, r, o);
28432 }

29028 const Self& add_if(bool cond, flecs::entity_t first, flecs::entity_t second) const {
29029 if (cond) {

29031 } else {
29032 /* If second is 0 or if relationship is exclusive, use wildcard for
29033 * second which will remove all instances of the relationship.
29034 * Replacing 0 with Wildcard will make it possible to use the second
29035 * as the condition. */
29036 if (!second || ecs_has_id(this->world_, first, flecs::Exclusive)) {
29037 second = flecs::Wildcard;
29038 }
29039 return this->remove(first, second);
29040 }
